entries.reason: REVIEWED 2026-10-15 (was 'unreviewed' since the gate was seeded 2026-09-23). No better mechanism exists today, measured rather than assumed: (1) `uninstall quit:` addresses NSApplications by bundle id, and BOTH helpers are bare binaries, not applications -- `divoomd` carries an embedded `__TEXT,__info_plist` with CFBundleIdentifier com.divoom.divoomd (verified with otool on the shipped Divoom.app), but that plist exists for macOS Bluetooth TCC attribution and does not register the process with LaunchServices, so `quit:` cannot reach it; `divoom-menubar` has no plist section at all. (2) The menubar agent is spawned detached (start_new_session) and orphans to launchd when the GUI quits, so it has no LaunchAgent to unload either. (3) There is no pidfile: the daemon's stable handle is the /tmp/divoom.sock control socket, which carries no process identity. The pattern is as narrow as the need: -f matches the full command line, and the string is the installed app's own helper path, so it cannot match the main app at Contents/MacOS/Divoom; `|| true` makes a no-match a non-failure. The REAL fix needs divoom-control to give the helpers a stable identity -- a LaunchAgent, or a pidfile -- and that is recorded in ROADMAP T2.3. RE-MEASURED 2026-10-19 against divoom-control v0.41.3: the reason still holds, so the pkill and this entry STAY. The menubar agent is still spawned detached (subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True) at divoom_gui/gui_main.py:467) and the daemon is spawned detached too (divoom_client/daemon_client.py:236); divoomd's embedded plist is still only a Bluetooth-TCC attribution plist (divoomd/build.rs) and divoom-menubar still has no plist section; there is still no pidfile and no LaunchAgent anywhere in divoom-control. The app's own shared-lifecycle quit path does terminate the menubar (divoom_gui/gui_main.py:_terminate_menubar_agent), but it is skipped when keep_daemon_alive is on and never runs if the GUI is killed, so the orphan case is real.
